# `Q-13-8` — Unsupported toc-location Value

> The `toc-location` option has a value Quarto does not support;
> a fallback placement is used.

## What this means

The `toc-location` option controls where the table of contents is
placed in HTML output:

```yaml
toc: true
toc-location: left
```

Supported values are `left`, `right` (the default), and `body`.
This warning fires when the option carries any other value. The
document still renders, with a fallback placement:

- `left-body` falls back to `left`, and `right-body` falls back
  to `right`. These two values (which in Quarto 1 render a
  sidebar TOC *plus* a copy in the document body) are not
  implemented yet.
- Any other value falls back to the default, `right`.

## Why this happens

Either a typo (`toc-location: lft`), or use of the `left-body` /
`right-body` double-TOC values, which Quarto 2 does not implement
yet.

## How to fix

Use one of the supported values:

```yaml
toc-location: left   # TOC in a left sidebar
toc-location: right  # TOC in the right margin (default)
toc-location: body   # TOC at the top of the document body
```

If you need the `left-body` / `right-body` double-TOC behavior,
follow Quarto 2 development — until it lands, the sidebar half of
the value is honored.
